text:
andrew: quick sync - after yesterday's kernel selector tweak we shipped, infra telemetry shows host CPU p99 up ~20% for workloads dominated by short chats (<25 tokens). p50 unchanged. suspect host-side string work and write syscall churn.

sophie: can you paste the top hot functions from perf?

andrew: from a 3m capture on canary: 
```
host_tokenizer_ascii_fastpath 34.8%\nproto::Message::ParseFromArray 22.1%\nutf8_normalize 11.3%\ngrpc::internal::Writev 9.6%\nkv_cache::evict_cycle 6.2%\nscheduler::kernel_select 3.0%\nothers 13.0%
```

mike: interesting that ascii fastpath is highest - maybe tokenize allocs are heavy when not cached. also proto parse high due to reflection path for repeated top-level fields.

lee: writev at ~10% and avg write size 200 bytes => syscall overhead visible. traces show many responses do 2 writes: header then payload.

andrew: quick microbench: single short request path baseline before kernel change: host CPU p99 ~120ms. after kernel change p99 ~145ms. run shows 22% increase.

sophie: two-prong mitigation plan: (1) micro-optimizations on host paths: introduce pooled token buffers + skip-normalize for ascii-only inputs, inline proto decode for common shapes; (2) IO coalescing: small write aggregator at host edge that defers flush up to 1.5ms or until 1KB threshold.

mike: inline proto decode: i can generate static decoders for the top 4 request variants used by short-chat. avoids reflection & bigint checks. will bench.

lee: coalescer: low-risk implementation idea: per-connection buffer + timer; configurable via feature flag. canary with 1ms delay gives 60% reduction in smallwrite ratio in local sim. downside: adds 1ms tail if buffer not filled. for short-chat p99 reduction might be worth it.

ops-bot: note - KV cache eviction spikes detected at 2024-04-06T10:14:xxZ (canary group). evictions/sec up 4.8x vs baseline.

andrew: lee - can you also look at connection-level batching heuristics to avoid cross-request stalls? maybe batch until end-of-stream or a short timer.

lee: yep. proposing adaptive timer: start at 0.5ms under low qps, shrink to 0.2ms when qps high. threshold tuning in console.

sophie: tokenizer fastpath: i'll add an ascii-only codepath that uses stack buffer for <=64 bytes and avoids heap allocs. also add pretokenized LRU for repeated tiny prompts (cache key = route+hash). risk: memory increase; suggest small cache (~128 entries) per host.

mike: kernel fallback: we should add rule in kernel-selector: if seq_len < 40 use short-seq kernel. makes sense to avoid moving CPU to host. small cost for longer seqs negligible. I'll add in selector config and a canary.

andrew: telemetry changes: add host.parse_cpu_by_route, smallwrite_ratio_by_route, kv.eviction_rate. include these in per-route dashboards and perf alerts.

infra-bot: canary deploy scheduled: infra-service v2.19.0 -> canary subset (flags: coalescer=true, ascii-fastpath=false, kv-bump=true)

andrew: starting perf capture now. will post pprof + flamegraph in ~12m. tagging @sophie @mike @lee.

~12m later~

andrew: initial canary numbers: p99 host CPU down from 145ms -> 128ms (11.7% improvement) with coalescer=true + kv bump. smallwrite ratio dropped 72% -> 28%. kv.evictions back to baseline. proto parse still heavy.

sophie: good win. coalescer clearly helps. next step: enable ascii-fastpath in canary and re-run.

mike: inline proto patch ready for bench. locally reduced parse CPU by ~35% on synthetic of common shape. will open PR for review.

lee: i'll tweak adaptive timer values and add observability for coalescer-induced latency. want to ensure tail doesn't regress for interactive flows.

andrew: agreed. plan for next 48 hours: (1) enable ascii-fastpath in canary + run perf (owner @sophie), (2) merge inline proto patch behind flag and A/B (owner @mike), (3) add kernel fallback rule for short seqs (owner @mike), (4) monitor kv.evictions and host.parse_cpu in console (owner @lee).

sophie: taking (1). aiming to have canary toggle by EOD.

mike: taking (2) and (3). will coordinate rollout with infra.

infra-bot: canary update: coalescer=true, ascii-fastpath=true, kv-bump=true applied to group-2 at 2024-04-06T10:50:00Z

andrew: latest canary run with ascii-fastpath on: p99 host CPU down to 112ms vs prior 145ms (22.7% total improvement). tokenization CPU share reduced from 34.8% -> 8.5%. proto parse still ~18%.

sophie: great. combined wins look solid. next: we should scope tokenizer pool memory usage and set LRU size by route weight. also add a datadog alert if pool miss rate > 10%.

lee: coalescer tail observed +0.6ms in worst-case synthetic but overall p99 improved. we'll keep adaptive timer.

andrew: leaving this thread as the single source for follow-ups. will open PR links and perf artifacts here. thanks all. :rocket:
